issues.what: OCR returned E11 with 'UNITED' (13.8-20.0 s) and 'STAT' (16.5-20.0 s), and ASR returned 'failed'. W1 never read E11, and the report never mentions the on-screen text or the ASR failure. The in-loop downgrade then had to add 'What the video as a whole shows and says (speech, on-screen text) is not reported'.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches running content tools and then ignoring what they return, and silently dropping a tool failure.
issues.ideal: Read E11 (or quote the OCR summary) and report the aircraft markings with their times. Add a limitation that ASR failed, so speech is unknown, not absent.

issues.what: The task is about provenance and identity. The frames show the boarding person, but neither workspace ran an image search on any keyframe (E3-E10/E12), and nothing was ever compared with a reported copy. Both reports then say 'no examined source correspondence identifies the person boarding as Harris'.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches declaring identity and event correspondence undeterminable without trying the one tool that could establish them.
issues.ideal: Run SEARCH image on a clear boarding frame (e.g. E5/E8). Open a matching news or agency copy and check that it corresponds before stating identity or event.

issues.what: The T1 text asks W2 to 'Examine the complete 20.218-second video E1 ... Establish through source correspondence whether the person boarding is Harris', but the Scope lists only 'open and read' the C-SPAN and DVIDS pages. W2 did exactly those four actions and reported after 5 of 12 turns. It never touched the video and never searched.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: The round-2 Scope chases the leftover 'unread pages' and skips the main gaps the downgrade named (video content, identity), so round 2 cannot close them.
issues.ideal: Put the video items first in the Scope (read OCR E11, retry ASR, image-search a keyframe) and drop or deprioritise a page whose title is obviously off-topic.

issues.what: The workspace opened and read the C-SPAN page 'User Clip: Border Czar Harris Appointed by Biden, Mar. 24, 2021'. Its R7 snippet already showed it was about the border assignment ('PRESIDENT BIDEN TASKED VICE PRESIDENT KAMALA HARRIS WITH SOLVING THE BORDER CRISIS').
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches reading pages that are visibly irrelevant just because they were listed as unread.
issues.ideal: Skip it, noting the snippet shows it is off-topic, and spend the turn on the video or an image search.

issues.what: The INCOMPLETE reason says 'Part 6—existing reporting: the contents of E14 and E15 were not examined in the supplied state'. W1 read both pages and the task passed them as materials. It also says 'the claim could not be verified', which retreats from W1's supported 'misleading' assessment. Every task part is listed as unresolved in a boilerplate pattern.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches false or boilerplate limitations and treats evidence already gathered as missing, which pushes the agent toward empty INCOMPLETE reports.
issues.ideal: Carry the W1 findings from E14/E15 forward and state only the gaps that are really open (identity, full video content), each tied to the step that was not done.

issues.what: The query 'Pentagon John Kirby March 24 2021 vice president Kamala Harris no requirement salute' includes the name 'John Kirby', which appears in no visible observation before this step. Kirby first shows up in the R4/R8 snippets returned by the next search, at turn 9.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: If Kirby is not in the truncated E15 text, the student learns to inject a spokesperson's name from world knowledge.
issues.ideal: Use only visible cues, e.g. 'Pentagon statement vice president not required to return salutes Harris Air Force Two'.

issues.what: The query 'site.defense.gov March 24 2021 Kirby briefing ...' uses a malformed operator ('site.' instead of 'site:') and over-stuffs it with terms. The results were mostly the same pages again (R1, R4, R6) plus an irrelevant C-SPAN clip.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches broken search syntax and near-duplicate queries.
issues.ideal: Write 'site:defense.gov Kirby salute vice president' or use a different angle (e.g. the AP fact-check R6).

issues.what: Visible snippets R4 ('The March 19 video shows the VP walking past saluting ...') and R6 ('failed to salute ... boarding Air Force Two on March 19 in Georgia. AP'S ASSESSMENT: False') were never used. The report says the recording date and event are not established and does not note that fact-checks place the event on March 19.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches dropping visible, relevant, attributable evidence (an independent fact-check verdict and the reported event date).
issues.ideal: Add a finding attributed to snippet level: AP and WUSA9 report the video as March 19 boarding of Air Force Two and rate the claim false. Pages failed to load, so this is snippet only.

issues.what: The verifier fed back five 'unsupported_assertion/critical' issues and one 'attribution_drift/major', yet the exported 'REVISED ANSWER' is word-for-word identical to the original ANSWER.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: The exported answer either still has issues the verifier flagged as critical, or the revise step is a no-op. Either way the training target is unreconciled with the verifier.
issues.ideal: Revise the flagged sentences (e.g. tie 'misleading' to E15's quoted Pentagon statement and reword attributions), or exclude the run if the verifier was wrong.

issues.what: T1 copies the full task verbatim with no decomposition. The QUERY_MEMORY query is a truncated task prefix: 'Fact-check the following claim, which circulated as the title of'.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches no decomposition and memory queries that carry no content.
issues.ideal: Split T1 into video content, identity/provenance and protocol/motive parts, and query memory with content terms (e.g. 'W1 salute findings E14 E15').

good_patterns: Rationales and findings consistently separate an absent or unreturned salute from deliberate refusal or motive, and call 'disgraceful' an opinion instead of over-asserting.

Dates are handled carefully: F5 notes the 2021-03-23 posting date is supplied by the task and does not establish the recording date, and F2 in W2 does not treat the DVIDS briefing date as the video's date.
W2 findings are faithful to page text and numerically correct (DVIDS 'Length: 00:46:13' -> '46 minutes 13 seconds'; date taken/posted 03.23.2021).
The failed-page count in the W1 limitation (4 of 8 candidates failed: R3, R4, R5, R6) is accurate and stated explicitly.
cannot_judge: Whether 'John Kirby' appears in the truncated remainder of E15 (+4399 chars) visible to the student at turn 8.
Where '20.218-second' in the round-2 task comes from: not in the rendered observations ('0-20 s', 'median shot 20.2 s'), possibly in the material metadata cards.
Whether the E12 frame description in W1 F2 (arms lowered, personnel holding salutes) matches the pixels; only the label is rendered.
Whether the verifier's five critical unsupported_assertion flags were correct, since the specific sentences are not shown.
summary: The rationales are cautious and the claim analysis is well separated (absent salute vs refusal vs motive). But the trajectory never uses its own OCR output, never reports the ASR failure, and never image-searches a keyframe, then declares identity and event correspondence undeterminable. The round-2 Scope chases two unread pages (one obviously off-topic) instead of the video gaps, and W2 ends with a boilerplate INCOMPLETE that falsely says E14/E15 were not examined. The exported FINISH answer is identical to the pre-verification answer despite five critical verifier flags.
